title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 186
paragraphs: With the fighting force at this number, the attendants who accompanied them and the men in the small vessels that carried grain, along with those in the other vessels that sailed with the army — I suppose these were not fewer than the fighting men but more. I will assume them to be equal in number, neither more nor less; and so, being equal in number to the fighting body, they make up the same total. Thus 5,283,220 was the number of men whom Xerxes son of Darius led as far as Sepias and Thermopylae.
